discovery: Development of next-generation (massively parallel sequencing-by-synthesis) DNA sequencing technology
rationale: Solexa/Illumina sequencing-by-synthesis, which uses reversible dye terminators on clonal clusters, cut genome sequencing costs by orders of magnitude and changed biology and medicine. Its inventors have already received major precursor awards (the Breakthrough Prize and the Millennium Technology Prize). Their field has not been honored yet, while recent Chemistry prizes went to MOFs (2025), protein design (2024) and quantum dots (2023). That makes a chemistry-of-life-sciences tool award plausible.
